## Findings by module

### 2

- **contradicted** (ch-002.txt): Kenya TJRC (2013) says the Mau Mau 'caused the death of at least 14,000 Africans, 29 Asians and 95 Europeans' while calling the figures debatable; the course uses Reader/Anderson counts of about 2,000 loyalist Kikuyu and 32 white civilians. The TJRC text is a compilation of secondary writers without a method, and its 14,000 may include Kikuyu killed in the wider war. Keep the course figures, flag the TJRC range as a contested compilation [CONTESTED]
- **contradicted** (ch-010.txt): Kenya TJRC chapter 4 on Lari corrects the TJRC's own chapter 1: the first Lari massacre (night of 25-26/03/1953, Mau Mau attackers killing loyalist families) left about 75 (Evans's count) to 120 dead, and the second (26-27/03/1953, home guards, police and reservists) left more than 200 bodies, an official 150 'alleged participants' killed, and about 400 by Anderson's reckoning (at least two for each in the first). Chapter 1's 'about 400 killed at Lari, mostly women and children' joins the two episodes and wrongly gives the second toll to the first [CONTESTED]; about 70 men were hanged after trials of about 2,000 suspects (12 on 15/10/1953)
- **extended** (ch-002.txt): TJRC: Corfield Tribunal recorded 11,503 Mau Mau dead (probably an undercount); about 1,000 hanged; 150,000 to 320,000 detained in more than 50 camps; Lari, 26/03/1953, about 400 killed, mostly women and children; Hola 1959, 11 detainees clubbed to death and 77 permanently injured. It follows Elkins, Anderson and Hornsby. It dates the war 1952-55 in one place and ends it with Kimathi in 10/1956, so its own dates differ
- **extended** (ch-002.txt): TJRC: the British removed and hid most records of the war on the eve of independence; Kenyatta's government did not honour Mau Mau, amnesty for fighters ran to 01/1964 (over 2,000 surrendered), and the 2011 British court ruling let Kenyan claimants sue. The Commission traces Mau Mau to land alienation: Crown Lands Ordinance 1915, about 5 million acres taken by 1914, about 294,000 Kikuyu outside the reserves in 1948 (29 per cent)
- **extended** (ch-010.txt): Kenya TJRC chapter 4 on Hola and the camps: 11 detainees beaten to death, announced 04/03/1959 as deaths from a water cart (camp commandant Sullivan's false account); Goudie inquiry found death from violence (18/03/1959); about 52,000 men in custody by end 1954 after Operation Anvil (05-06/1954); about 50,000 released in 1957, leaving about 30,000 hard-core; 'dilution' beatings and Operation Progress; a typhoid outbreak at Manyani killed about 60; the Cabinet-level cover-up ended British claims of moral fitness to rule. The same chapter says the Shifta War state of emergency in the North East lasted to 1991

### 4

- **extended** (ch-002.txt): TJRC on independent Kenya: independence 12/12/1963, republic with Kenyatta as President a year later (confirms the course's check on Reader); Pio Gama Pinto killed 24/02/1965, Tom Mboya 05/07/1969, Kisumu shootings 25/10/1969, J M Kariuki 1975; one-party state de jure from 1982 and ended 1991; 1982 coup attempt cost an estimated 600 to 1,800 lives

Totals: 0 confirmed, 0 refined, 2 contradicted, 4 extended, 0 absent, 0 note.
